Weight vectors of the published quantile-based estimators and the BLUE

Source: R/weights.R
estimator_weights.Rd

Returns the weight vector \(w\) such that the estimator is \(w'Y\), with \(Y\) the reported values in increasing order (for example the minimum, the median and the maximum under S1). All formulas were read from the source PDFs.

Usage

estimator_weights(
  n,
  scenario = c("S3", "S1", "S2", "S4", "S5"),
  estimand = c("mean", "sd"),
  method = c("blue", "luo", "wan", "shi"),
  moments = NULL,
  type = 7
)

Arguments

n

A single integer sample size. The Wan, Luo and Shi presets are closed forms in \(n\) and accept any \(n \ge 2\); the BLUE needs the sample sizes of imputed_moments.

scenario

Character. One of "S1" (min, median, max), "S2" (three quartiles), "S3" (all five). McGrath 2023 labels; note Wan 2014's C2/C3 are S3/S2 respectively. Also "S4" (the quartiles with the 10th and 90th percentiles) and "S5" (all five with the two percentiles), the names of Wu, Shi and Tong (2026) for Scenarios 5 and 7 of Balakrishnan et al. (2022); only the BLUE ("blue") is defined for these two.

estimand

"mean" or "sd".

method

One of the following; "blue" is the default. Under S4 and S5 only "blue".

"blue"

The default. Lloyd's generalized-least-squares best linear unbiased estimator computed from the exact means and covariance matrix of the reported values (Balakrishnan 2022 eqs. 8-9; Yang 2022 Definition 3.1).

"wan"

The estimators used/recommended in Wan et al. (2014). Mean: Hozo's \((a+2m+b)/4\) for S1 (Wan eq. 3), \((q_1+m+q_3)/3\) for S2 (Wan eq. 14), Bland's \((a+2q_1+2m+2q_3+b)/8\) for S3 (Wan eq. 10). SD: \((b-a)/\xi_B(n)\) for S1 (eq. 9), \((q_3-q_1)/\eta_B(n)\) for S2 (eq. 16), the average of the two for S3 (eq. 13), with Blom-approximated divisors \(\xi_B(n) = 2\Phi^{-1}\{(n-0.375)/(n+0.25)\}\), \(\eta_B(n) = 2\Phi^{-1}\{(0.75n-0.125)/(n+0.25)\}\).

"luo"

Mean only. Luo et al. (2018) eqs. (7), (11), (15): S1 \(w_1 = 4/(4+n^{0.75})\) on the mid-range; S2 \(w = 0.7+0.39/n\) on the mid-quartile range; S3 \(w_1 = 2.2/(2.2+n^{0.75})\), \(w_2 = 0.7-0.72/n^{0.55}\).

"shi"

SD only, S3 only. Shi et al. (2020) eqs. (5), (9), (10): weight \(w = 1/(1+0.07 n^{0.6})\) on \((b-a)/\xi_B\), rest on \((q_3-q_1)/\eta_B\). For S1/S2 Shi recommends Wan's estimators.

moments

Optional precomputed result of osmoments::os_moments(n, ranks) for the standard normal, at this n and at the ranks that the reported values use (at n = 4Q+1 under type 7 these are scenario_ranks(n, scenario)), or a list with its components alpha and B alone. The sample size, the distribution, the ranks, the location and scale and the shape of alpha and B are checked where the object carries them; a bare list is checked for its size only. The package keeps the moments it computes itself for the session, so repeated calls at one sample size integrate once without this argument.

type

The definition of the sample quantiles, an integer from 1 to 9 as in quantile; 7, R's default, unless a study states another.

Value

Named numeric weight vector over the reported values, in increasing order, named as the scenario reports them: a the minimum, p10 the 10th percentile, q1, m the median, q3, p90 the 90th percentile and b the maximum.

Details

The Wan/Luo/Shi weights are closed-form functions of \(n\) and are returned for any single integer \(n \ge 2\), as the source papers apply them. The "blue" weights are computed from the exact means and covariance matrix of the reported values at any \(n\) (see imputed_moments, argument type) and use moments.

References

Wu Z, Shi J, Tong T (2026). Precision of the imputed mean and standard deviation from a five-number summary. Manuscript.

Examples

estimator_weights(25, "S3", "mean")           # the BLUE of the mean, the default
#>          a         q1          m         q3          b 
#> 0.08214526 0.28565964 0.26439020 0.28565964 0.08214526 
estimator_weights(25, "S3", "sd")             # the BLUE of the SD
#>             a            q1             m            q3             b 
#> -1.712665e-01 -2.565653e-01 -2.315005e-16  2.565653e-01  1.712665e-01 
estimator_weights(25, "S3", "mean", "luo")
#>          a         q1          m         q3          b 
#> 0.08221017 0.28870353 0.25817261 0.28870353 0.08221017 
estimator_weights(25, "S3", "sd", "shi")
#>          a         q1          m         q3          b 
#> -0.1716592 -0.2559979  0.0000000  0.2559979  0.1716592
